author: Russell Brand
description:
Dr. Stella Immanuel tells Russell why her views on childhood vaccination changed so dramatically, saying she would no longer take or administer another shot without stronger evidence convincing her of its benefits.

The conversation moves into her concerns about rising autism diagnoses, ADHD, SIDS and chronic illness, as well as her belief that Amish communities offer an important comparison because of differences in lifestyle and healthcare practices. Russell listens as Dr. Immanuel explains why these observations led her to question assumptions she once accepted as a trained pediatrician.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to the growing tension around protest, online speech and working-class activism in Britain. From masked protesters in Portsmouth to people being questioned over Facebook posts, the conversation asks a bigger question: how much freedom do you really have if authorities decide which forms of protest and speech are acceptable?

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to an old BBC interview where a string of elderly Brits list off their go to remedies for absolutely everything, whiskey in your tea, whiskey in your porridge, whiskey straight, boiled onions, and the occasional fist fight in the garden for good measure. It's a genuinely hilarious watch, closing with the perfect deadpan line, that's what was holding Britain together, but we beat Hitler.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell reacts to Nancy Pelosi's viral "No Kings" moment tearing up a paper crown in protest, and argues she'd be better served turning that same energy inward. Instead of the theatrics, he suggests she have an honest conversation with herself in the mirror about trading on information gained through her time in Congress, and about actually doing something for children rather than invoking them as a talking point whenever it's convenient. A sharp, pointed response to a viral political moment.
